title: IT / Finance / Security Admin Sync
summary: Monthly cross-team sync to review upcoming finance commitments, IT maintenance windows, and outstanding security/compliance items (SOC2 evidence, KMS rotation). Agreed on a short maintenance window on 2026-07-25, finance to approve split billing for Dedicated clusters, security to publish updated audit playbook. Action items agreed and owners assigned.
next_steps: AI: Finance to approve Dedicated cluster billing split by 2026-07-20
IT: Schedule 2-hour maintenance window on 2026-07-25 and publish runbook
Security: Publish KMS rotation plan and update audit playbook by 2026-07-22
Ops: Share low-risk dev checklist and link to runbook
action_items: Ava Thompson: Approve Dedicated billing split; due 2026-07-20
Liam O'Connor: Schedule maintenance window and circulate runbook; due 2026-07-18
Priya Singh: Publish KMS rotation timeline and audit playbook draft; due 2026-07-22
Carlos Gomez: Clean up service account RBAC and provide change log; due 2026-07-30
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-15
Start: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~45 minutes
Attendees: Maya P., Jordan L., Carlos G., Ava T., Liam O., Priya S., Elena R.

[00:00] Maya: Okay, hey everyone, thanks for joining. Uh, quick roll call — we have finance, IT, security, compliance — cool. I'll kick off with the agenda: billing split for Dedicated clusters, proposed maintenance window, KMS rotation, and SOC2 evidence backlog. Anything else?

[00:22] Ava: No that's good. I just want to make sure the finance ask about split billing is clear — we need line itemized costs per business unit for next quarter.

[00:35] Liam: And I'll need to know the maintenance window so I can plan backups and inform the SREs. ideally a 2 hour window late night.

[00:48] Priya: From security side, KMS rotation and audit logs — we still have a couple of outstanding evidence packets that the auditor asked about, so want to prioritize that.

[01:02] Maya: Great. Ok first topic, Dedicated billing. Ava, can you summarize finance needs?

[01:18] Ava: Sure. So we are being asked by finance leadership to show per-team usage for the Dedicated capacity. For procurement we need to map cost centers; the ask is: show per-cluster and per-namespace cost breakdowns, ideally exportable CSV. Also, we want a proposal on split billing — is it prorated by vGPU hours or by token consumption? Historically we billed raw hours but with Redwood's batching optimizations, token-based might make more sense but it's new to the controller.

[02:05] Jordan: Right, the batching and KV cache effects can skew raw hours vs effective usage. We can generate a vGPU-hour metric but it'll look different than per-token costs; also caching makes some workloads cheaper.

[02:21] Carlos: We have the usage logs — I'm fairly sure we can produce a CSV with vGPU hours and a second CSV with estimated token-based cost using the runtime metrics. Might need a small ETL job. I can own a PoC.

[02:40] Ava: Great. timeline?

[02:46] Carlos: I can put together an initial export by 2026-07-18, then iterate.

[02:52] Ava: That's tight but fine. thanks.

[03:00] Maya: Cool, next maintenance window — Liam?

[03:08] Liam: We propose Saturday July 25th 02:00-04:00 AM PT for the low-traffic window. We'll need 2 hours for kernel updates, container runtime bumps, and a quick smoke test. We'll publish the runbook.

[03:28] Priya: Quick question — will any keys be rotated during that window? If so we need to coordinate KMS and service account handoffs.

[03:37] Liam: No key rotation planned for that window; we're just patching nodes. But we will restart some inference nodes which may evict KV caches briefly. There's a potential temporary latency spike.

[03:52] Ava: Does that impact billing or SLA credits? We need to be careful for production customers.

[03:59] Maya: This is internal infra maintenance; we've scoped it as a low-risk window. We'll set the status page notice and make sure external tenants are unaffected — there is a fallback routing policy to regional spare capacity.

[04:18] Elena: From compliance angle, capture the maintenance runbook and pre/post checklists. auditors like to see change records.

[04:28] Liam: Absolutely. I'll create a change request in our tracker and link the runbook.

[04:35] Maya: Next KMS rotation — Priya?

[04:42] Priya: We're aiming for a quarterly KMS rotation for all customer-facing keys. The next window we've proposed is two weeks after the maintenance, so earliest 2026-08-08. We need to confirm service account permissions, and also check that any on-prem/private deployments have their own rotation schedule.

[05:02] Carlos: For Private deployments, customers manage their own KMS; we only manage keys for hosted/Dedicated. We should document the scope clearly so finance/procurement knows which product lines are affected.

[05:18] Ava: Ok. also for SOC2 evidence, the auditor asked for proof of periodic key rotation and the ticket trail. We need to gather past 12 months of rotation logs.

[05:32] Priya: I can get the rotation logs; though some of the older entries are in the legacy vault system — expect a little cleanup. I'll produce a consolidated CSV by 2026-07-22.

[05:49] Jordan: Note, some services had manual rotations and the notes weren't standard — machine readable evidence is better. We'll push a template for rotation evidence that includes key ID, rotated_at, rotated_by, and ticket ID.

[06:04] Maya: Good. Next, SOC2 evidence backlog — Elena, what's outstanding?

[06:11] Elena: We have two open items: 1) incident response drill evidence for Q1 and Q2, and 2) third-party vendor risk assessments missing signatures. Auditors asked to see proof that we executed tabletop for Q2.

[06:28] Priya: We ran a partial drill but the note-taking was sparse. I can reconstruct the timeline but will need others to confirm attendance.

[06:38] Ava: Finance needs to know if any vendor contracts will require budget approvals to complete the vendor assessments.

[06:45] Elena: A few assessments require procurement to pull contracts — I will send a list.

[06:50] Maya: Action item — Elena to send vendor list by end of week.

[06:57] Elena: Yep.

[07:00] Maya: Service account RBAC cleanup — Carlos?

[07:06] Carlos: We found ~23 service accounts with overly broad roles. We'll run a least-privileged audit and propose new role mappings. The plan is to do the audit, stage the changes in a dev cluster, and then roll out. This might take till end of month.

[07:20] Priya: Please ensure anything touching production has a rollback plan.

[07:25] Carlos: Of course. I'll include a rollback and change window.

[07:30] Maya: A few quick clarifications from the chat — someone mentioned Redwood Dedicted in the notes, that's a typo. Also the KV cash reference came up in earlier tickets (should be KV cache).

[07:42] Jordan: ha, classic transcription errors.

[07:46] Maya: Misc items — payroll integration for contractor billing, Ava?

[07:51] Ava: We're about to finalize contractor billing for Q3 and need export of usage for a small set of Dedicated infra usage. I'll request a scoped export for contractor cost centers and then we can push invoices.

[08:05] Carlos: I'll provide the export, same ETL work I'm doing for the broader split billing.

[08:10] Maya: Ok, let's go through action items and owners. I will record them in the tracker.

[08:18] (Fast recap from Maya)

[08:25] Maya: Ava — approve billing split by 2026-07-20. Liam — schedule maintenance window and publish runbook by 2026-07-18. Priya — KMS rotation timeline and consolidated rotation logs by 2026-07-22. Carlos — export CSVs and RBAC cleanup plan by 2026-07-30. Elena — vendor list and SOC2 outstanding items by 2026-07-17.

[08:50] Ava: Sounds good. Also, can we get a cost estimate for potential SLA credits if maintenance impacts external customers?

[08:58] Maya: We'll keep the window internal and use fallback capacity; but if you need a formal estimate, Carlos and Jordan can collaborate and provide one by next week.

[09:12] Jordan: Yep I'll work with Carlos.

[09:18] Liam: One last thing — we should add the maintenance notice to the ops calendar and status page. I'll do that after the runbook is ready.

[09:26] Maya: Perfect. Any other questions?

[09:30] Ava: None from finance.

[09:32] Priya: Nothing else.

[09:34] Elena: No.

[09:35] Maya: Alright thanks all. I'll send notes, and link the runbook and the ETL ticket. Meeting adjourned.

End of transcript.

Notes: transcription contains minor name misspellings (Dedicted / KV cash) — left intentionally to reflect auto-transcribed audio. Shared artifacts: runbook draft link: https://redwood.internal/runbooks/maintenance-2026-07-25, ETL ticket: https://redwood.internal/tickets/ETL-4321, SOC2 evidence tracker: https://redwood.internal/compliance/soc2-evidence
